title: The Book Nobody Kept
narration_slice: Beneath the spells and horns, however, darker whispers persisted concerning blood magic. Thousands of years after Valyria's rise, Septon Barth—Hand to King Jaehaerys the Conciliator and perhaps the keenest student of dragonkind Westeros ever produced—dared to write in his *Unnatural History* that Valyrian bloodmages had delved into forbidden secrets…
filing_note: Batch 055 frames are on disk under assets/batch_055/ and upload to their own Drive folder, EP001_BATCH_055_IMG0541-0550.
the_testimony_rule: **The past is never rendered as truth, only as testimony.** Barth is the frame, not the subject. Where Valyria appears it is small, partial or mediated — a wall the spells were spoken against, a city four thousand years dead, one woman seen from behind. There is no full-stage altar tableau and no centred mage.
the_paper_rule: The scholar's world is ink, foxing, broken cord, snapped seals and hands. **No glowing script, no floating glyphs, no illuminated sigils, no candles arranged for atmosphere.** Across five approved frames not one word resolves at 4x-5x magnification — checked on the near piles in 0543 and on the loose sheet in the 0543 pass-1 reject.
the_face_rule: Held again, and broken twice under new disguises: a **distant** seated figure in 0543 pass 1 whose head was a clean profile at 6x, and a **hand** in 0545 pass 1 that read as raw flesh. Both re-rendered. The rule now covers distance and skin, not just framing.
rejections_this_batch: IMG0543 pass 1 — seated figure at the far end of the table resolved into a full profile (nose, mouth, jaw) at 6x. Face rule. Re-rendered with the room emptied.
IMG0545 pass 1 — fingertips rendered deep red and read as bloodied flesh at 4x, contradicting the bible's 'faintly stained' and the no-injury line. Re-rendered with pale dry skin and soot grime.
IMG0546 — first generation call returned a failure (no image). Retried; the retry landed first look. Not a QC reject, a production miss.
IMG0548 pass 1 — close-cropped grey head turned away, but the EAR resolved crisply at 3x. The head must go outside the frame or be fully turned away. Re-rendered.

IMG0548 pass 2 — head removed, but a bare shoulder and the side of a neck sat in the left margin with the robe fallen off: undressed flesh at the frame edge. Re-rendered with the person removed entirely.
reframes_this_batch: IMG0546–IMG0550 delivered at 1672x941; resampled to 1376x768 via full-width preserve (no letterbox bands detected on any of the five).

scenes.visual_beat: Low-angle monumental architectural / geological framing — the wall the spells were spoken against
scenes.qc_note: LAM 28mm looking up a monumental wall of POURED FUSED black stone that runs out of frame. At 3x the surface is vertical frozen runs, flaking fracture plates and cooled flow sheets — **no courses, no blocks, no joint lines, no mortar**. A broad soot stain rises where heat has gone up the stone for generations: a stain, not a glow. One narrow cold grey shaft of daylight from high off-frame left skims the face and stops short of the floor. A bare stone step at the base is worn into a shallow dip by feet. Nothing alight, no symbols, no text, no figure.

scenes.visual_beat: Over-the-shoulder — the space where the horns were, and the book that replaced them
scenes.qc_note: OTS 40mm from behind and above a seated figure at a plain wooden table. At 4x the crop holds **only the back of a close-cropped grey head** — no face, no profile, no ear detail that resolves into a cheek. The subject of the frame is an **empty rectangle of clean unfaded wood** where a long object was lifted away, its edges sharper than the grime around it, one shallow impression in the dust beside it, a bronze stylus and a cloth-wrapped bundle tied with cord. Nothing on the walls. One dim lamp off-frame right puts a low warm edge on the table; the far wall stays in shadow. This is the whole thesis of the batch in one object: the horns are gone, the ledger of them remains.

scenes.visual_beat: Deep-focus wide atmospheric composition — the copies, and how many of them there were
scenes.rerender_of: Re-render of pass 1, which placed a seated figure at the far end whose head resolved at 6x into a clean profile — nose, mouth, jaw in silhouette. Distance is not an exemption from the no-face rule. Pass 2 empties the room entirely and turns the near leaves face-down. Also reframed: delivered letterboxed, cropped 14px top / bottom band and rescaled to 1376x768.
scenes.qc_note: WS 28mm down a long scriptorium table that runs away into shadow. Dozens of flat piles of bound sheets, corded bundles, wax seals in red and ochre, leaves curling at the corners, a pile tipped askew, sheets on the floor. At 5x the near leaves are **blank toned paper, foxing and shadow — no word, letter or rule resolves anywhere**. Two hands enter at the near end, one flat on a bundle, cuff of dark wool; hands only. **No person anywhere in the frame.** One high cold window slot lays a pale band along the table. The scale is administrative, not ceremonial: this is a library being counted, not an altar.

scenes.visual_beat: Ultra-wide establishing vista — the city four thousand years on
scenes.rerender_of: Reframed: delivered letterboxed, cropped 64px top / bottom band and rescaled to 1376x768.
scenes.qc_note: UWA 24mm from a high ridge in flat grey light. Middle distance: a great city reduced to **broken black walls, fallen spans, standing ribs and arched fragments**, half-swallowed in ash, rubble where streets ran — legible only as an absence with structure in it. At 4x the ruins are fracture and rubble, arches collapsed mid-span, no coursed elevation intact. **No fire, no smoke, no lights, no banners, no figures.** Foreground: raw rock, dry straw grass, one weathered surveyor's cairn of stacked flat stones. Sky heavy and even edge to edge, no sun, no shafts. The coldest frame in the episode.

scenes.visual_beat: Medium close-up — `CHAR-VAL-003` from behind, her hands and her hair doing the work
scenes.rerender_of: Re-render of pass 1, in which the fingertips rendered a deep red that read as raw flesh or blood at 4x. Pass 2 cools the hand to pale skin with soot grime only; braid, collar, bowl and wall carried over unchanged. Also reframed: delivered letterboxed, cropped 34px top / bottom band and rescaled to 1376x768.
scenes.qc_note: MCU 50mm from **directly behind and slightly above** the fire-mage: at 4x the frame holds a crown of coiled platinum braids wound with red-gold wire and two black glass pins, the nape, the standing collar of charcoal silk and deep red linen with bronze-thread embroidery, and the shard collar of volcanic glass and red gold. **No face, no profile, no eye, no cheek** — the woman is identified entirely by the back of her head and her hand. Her right hand rests open and spread on the ledge: pale, dry skin, **soot and grime at the nails and creases, no red, no blood, no wound**. Ahead of her an iron bowl of cold ash gives one thread of smoke. The wall behind is poured fused mass with frozen drips. Nothing glowing, no glyphs.

scenes.visual_beat: Dynamic medium lateral tracking angle — the destruction of the copies
scenes.qc_note: MS 35mm low on the lip of a sunken font of POURED FUSED monolith. Inside, cord-bound manuscripts already collapsed into black charcoal and pale grey ash; surviving flames hand-sized and CONTAINED inside the stone — no blaze, no fireball, no ember swarm, no sparks, no glow in the ash. One intact bundle on the rim, wax seal broken, pages blank at 6x (toned, foxed, no letter). One soot-blackened hand on the bundle — wrist and cuff of coarse wool only, no arm, no body, no face, and at 3x no red, no wound, no burn. Short bronze strike-ring and rod on the rim. Thin smoke drawn sideways by a draught. One cold grey daylight bar from a high slot across the near stones; beyond the font is black.

scenes.visual_beat: Compressed telephoto dramatic subject framing — what a scholar touches, and what it is made of
scenes.qc_note: MCU 65mm across the corner of a scrubbed table in low lamplight. Open bound volume, page toned and foxed: at 5x fibre, foxing and shadow, not one letter and not one ruled line. A curved shard of black dragonbone — dull iron-dark, fine lengthwise grain, worn chipped edge — lies on the page as a page-weight, the SAME material as the horns of 0517/0532, not an ornament and not a talisman. One pale dry deeply creased hand from the right, forefinger pressing the shard's ridge; at 3x pale and dry, no red, no blood, no wound, no burn, nail short and clean. Bronze rule and squat inkpot with cut-down quill just outside focus. Matte and dusty throughout, nothing alight beyond the off-frame lamp.

scenes.visual_beat: Medium cinematic subject focus — the room the book was written in, with the writer gone
scenes.qc_note: MS 50mm across an empty working study at shoulder height. NO person anywhere — not a hand, not a shoulder, not a head. Scrubbed table with a bound ledger open, pages blank at 5x (fibre and foxing, no word/rule/alphabet), broken cord and snapped seal beside it, quill upright in a squat inkpot, folded grey linen, small bronze rule, one loose sheet weighted flat. An EMPTY wooden stool pushed back at a slight angle, seat worn smooth in the middle by long use — the sitter is the seat's wear, not a body. Squat clay lamp at the right end, flame small and flat, contained in the vessel. Lime-plaster wall, patchy, flaking, soot-darkened at the crown; no coursed ashlar, no mortar joints, no brickwork. One narrow high slot lays a thin grey bar across the far wall and flagstones, worn into a shallow dip between stool and door.
scenes.rerender_of: TWO passes rejected. Pass 1: close-cropped grey head turned away, but at 3x the EAR resolved crisply — the brief must put the head outside the frame or fully turned away, not merely 'not a portrait'. Pass 2: head out, but a bare shoulder and the side of a neck sat in the left margin with the robe fallen away — undressed flesh at the frame edge, and a maester is a robed man. Pass 3 removes the person entirely: chair pushed back, page still open, lamp still burning.

scenes.visual_beat: Wide environmental storytelling tableau — the whole scriptorium, and how little of it there is
scenes.qc_note: WS 35mm from the dark of a doorway down a barrel-vaulted room. ONE seated figure at a table, seen entirely from behind and at distance — at 6x a soft circle of cropped grey hair over dark shoulders, no profile, no ear, no brow, no eye, no facial plane; the head is a shape, not a face, and it is the only figure in the room. Table: open ledger, inkpot, quill, two cord-bound bundles. Near-wall shelf of further corded bundles and stacked sheets — at 5x cord, paper edge and shadow, nothing legible. One clay lamp is the only warm light near the figure; one thin cold daylight bar from a high slit lies flat on the flagstones. Lime-plaster walls, patchy and soot-darkened, vault crown lost to pure black. Flagstones worn into a shallow dip between door and table. No marble, no columns, no coursed ashlar, no cobwebs, no candle array.

scenes.visual_beat: High-elevation geographic / scale reveal — the world the book describes, from a ridge, in flat light
scenes.qc_note: UWA 24mm from a bare limestone ridge. Middle distance: a small walled town of low stone houses with pitched slate and thatch roofs, a stub of a tower, one packed-earth road running out of it — geographically placed, small in frame, a settlement and not a fantasy castle; at 8x–9x it resolves into gabled roofs, dark window voids and drystone field walls, no banners, no heraldry, no glyph, no text. Dry tawny plain, scattered olive trees with dusty grey-green leaves, thin drystone walls, a pale braided river bed with very little water. Far distance: the sea, flat and leaden under heavy even overcast, with a level hard horizon — no sun, no shafts, no god-light, no stars, no moon. Foreground: fractured limestone, dry straw grass, one weathered cairn of stacked flat stones. No figures, no smoke, no fire, no ships, no modern objects.

batch_055_close_note: Batch 055 'The Book Nobody Kept' CLOSED 10/10. Five rejections across three frames (0543 profile at 6x, 0545 red fingertips at 4x, 0548 ear at 3x then bare shoulder at 2.5x) plus one transport failure on 0546. Every re-render passed first look on retry. The batch's argument holds across all ten frames: the past is testimony, never truth — an empty rectangle of unfaded wood where the horns were (0542), an administrative pile of copies (0543), a city four thousand years dead with nothing burning on it (0544), a woman identified only by the back of her head (0545), copies burned in a contained stone font (0546), a dragonbone shard used as a page-weight (0547), an empty stool still warm with use (0548), a poor vaulted room with one figure at distance (0549), and a small town in a large country under leaden overcast (0550).
batch_055_detail_lesson_2: The no-face rule is a CROP check, not a framing instruction, and it has a second clause: skin at the edge of frame is still a body, and a body without its robe is a continuity error rather than a camera angle. 0548 needed three passes — ear at 3x, then bare shoulder at 2.5x — before the reliable answer appeared: photograph the wear, not the wearer. The empty pushed-back stool is stronger than any figure and satisfies testimony perfectly.
fire_containment_rule: Fire is permitted only where a hand built a place to hold it, and the frame must show the containment as clearly as the fire. 0546's burning manuscripts survive the batch's no-glow rule because every flame is hand-sized and inside a stone-lined font; no blaze, no embers, no glow in the ash.
